What is the most obnoxious thing you have seen someone do at the grocery store? Our local version of Costco is called PriceSmart. Isn't that a clever name? A lady in front of me, at the queue to cash, decided she was cleverer than me and all the fine people employed at PriceSmart. To shop at PriceSmart you have to be a member. You do this by purchasing a membership subscription card which allows you a year of membership. For the average Joe it's a tad costly ($265 TT) but the savings you get shopping at PriceSmart, more than makes up for it. I'm a very economical shopper and I tend to purchase only the bare necessities and would treat myself to something nice only once in a blue moon. This lady in front of me had a cart piled with groceries and also several treats ranging from frozen salmon burgers, Lindt, Toblerone and Mars chocolates, smoked almonds and ribs. Clearly she was not a poor lady. When we neared the cashier she suddenly turned around to stare me in the eyes. This is the conversation that followed. Lady: You don't mind if I use your card right? Me: For what? Lady: To cash. Me: You don't have a card? Lady: No. Can't afford it. I then stared at her pile of groceries tethering at the edge of her trolley. Her bottle of Grey Goose Vodka was almost $300TT but she ‘couldn't afford' a $200TT (at that time) membership. Me: It's only $200 for the membership and it takes just a minute. I saw her face suddenly transform into a look of complete irritation. It was as if I was asking her for the favour. Lady: I don't have the money right now. I just told you. People need to help each other. Me: Well I can't lend you my card. Lady: Why? Me: Because I don't know you. Lady: You need to know me to help me? At that point I remained silent. I didn't want to call her out for attempting to use random strangers for her financial convenience. I didn't want to argue that I spent my hard earned money on this membership and she ought to make that sacrifice also rather than gorge on her four rotisserie chickens as it was not my place to say. Instead she went to the man in front of her, giving him a sad story of how she just lost her card and this stuff is for her mother. The guy took the bait and lent her his card. She then stared at me as if to say, 'Got anything to say now?’ Clearly this wasn't the first time she did this and it definitely wasn't going to be the last. Some people may not see the big deal of what happened there but to me she is trash: a selfish and cheap opportunist. She is a leech on PriceSmart (who generates a profit from membership fees) and on the good people around her who make the necessary sacrifices for the greater good. Edit 24.11.21 Whoa. 5K upvotes. I always thought venting anger never got people anywhere. Was wise enough to avoid that lady's scheme. Was not so wise as a teenager when I fell for a bootlegger's silly scam. Click here to read all about it.

What is the lamest “benefit” you’ve been offered by an employer? At Papa John’s Pizza (Trinidad) I was getting fed up that they weren't hiring the sufficient amount of staff to properly run the store. Along with doing bike deliveries I also cashed, took phone calls, entered orders, swept, mopped and emptied garbage. They kept a skeleton staff of 3 workers per shift and whenever they had to pay overtime they grumbled and wanted explanations as to why. Frustrated and fatigued I applied for Domino’s (Trinidad) Pizza delivery. This is how snippets of the conversation went during the interview. Interview Lady: We pay the highest hourly rate of all pizza restaurants. $21(TTD) per hour. Me: Papa John's paid $20 an hour. This is just a dollar more. Lady: Yes! The highest rate for delivery riders in the country! Lady: When you come to the restaurant you’ll be happy to see that you'll be getting so much deliveries. Endless deliveries! Me: How much do I get paid per delivery? Lady: $7 per delivery! Me: That's the lowest delivery payment of all the pizza restaurants. Lady: Yes but you'll be doing so many deliveries, getting so much tips that it wouldn't matter. (I later found out that Domino's charged customers $20 for delivery, the highest delivery charge of all fast food restaurants in the country. They paid the driver $7 out of the $20 charge and the restaurant pocketed the remaining $13 for themselves.) Me: What are the closing hours? Lady: 10:30pm. Me: You mean like only on Fridays and Saturdays? Lady: No every day. Me: Thats a bit late and taxis round here stop working around 8pm. Any transport provided for me to get home? Lady: No. Me: Will I be able to use the Domino's motorcycle to get home? (I was allowed this benefit in a previous restaurant I worked that had this same issue) Lady: No. Me: Can I leave earlier then? Lady: Of course. Due to your transport situation we’ll allow you to leave 10 minutes earlier! Lady: We are a very flexible organization. Me: How so? (inwardly groaning, expecting more bullshit) Lady: We give you the choice to work either as contracted or non-contracted. Me: What does that mean? Lady: Contracted means that you work somewhat as a permanent staff. You can work all the overtime hours you want. However overtime would be paid at the usual rate of $21 an hour. No time and a half. The same applies for public holidays. Non contracted is like temporary staff. We pay the usual time and a half for overtime but as you are non contracted you don't get overtime hours as we send you home after you've made your 40hrs a week. We don't allow you to work on holidays so you basically get your flat salary every week whereas with a contract you are allowed more hours. Me: More hours at the same rate? Lady: Yes. Me: Wouldn't that be a lose-lose situation? Lady: No. It's a win-win! Me: Am I entitled to a free meal? Lady: No. Me: And the uniform? Lady: We are the only pizza restaurant that provides free uniforms for staff? Me: How many uniforms? Lady: Two free Domino's shirts and a cap. We are having them laundered after being returned by a delivery driver who recently left. Me: You're giving me a guy's used clothes? No: No. She only used them for two days. They're practically new. Me: You're giving me used female clothing? Lady: It's a free uniform! Suffice to say I instantly and humbly returned to Papa John's and their skeleton staff. Edit: So as not to confuse anyone else, all rates here are in Trinidad dollars and not US. Approx 7TT = 1US. Edit: Not the first time a fast food restaurant tried to pull a fast one on its workers. Read here how one restaurant tried to borrow money from its workers in disguise.

At what age did you stop enjoying YA fiction? I'm not hating on YA authors but I never saw the appeal. As a child Roald Dahl was my favorite author. I also read abridged and illustrated editions of the popular classics from Mark Twain, H.G. Wells, Arthur Conan Doyle, Dickens etc. As I entered my teens I attempted unabridged editions of the classics and voraciously read through my mother's bookshelf of adult novels. In my late teens I fell in love with The Good Earth by Pearl S. Buck and Angela's Ashes by Frank McCourt. I discovered early that I had a passion for historical stories of persistence through hardship, survival etc. YA books, to me, were for the kids who didn't really have a passion for reading and were off to a late start. YA books never had the charisma and imagination of children's books nor did they have the depth and seriousness of adult novels. They were just generic books written for overly self aware kids imho. I know I may sound pompous but I really didn't want to read about rich kids in school, girls dating the bad boy, broken friendships, parents divorcing or a boy and his dog surviving in some post apocalyptic future. I know there are good YA books out there but I really haven't come across one that appealed to me nor am I interested in looking for one at this stage in my life.

Who is the best classic rock drummer? I tire of reading the same responses. Neil Peart John Bonham Keith Moon I love them all and they all have their own flavour but in terms of consistency of quality I'd go with this kraut. Jaki Liebezeit of CAN Tribal Pulsating Rolling Cerebral Motorik These are some of the adjectives used to describe his primordial style of playing. His style ranges from hypnotic (Oh Yeah) to furiously tribal (Mother Sky) to funky (Vitamin C) to airy and sophisticated (Future Days) and in many instances he incorporates all the above mentioned styles in just one epic song (Bel Air). He is the most idiosyncratic of all the classic rock drummers which isn't surprising coming from the most original band in rock history. A German artrock band with a Japanese lead singer whose freeform nonsensical lyrics are sometimes sung in his own coded language. I love CAN. For the period 1970 — 1975 they released six stunning albums (one each consecutive year) Soundtracks (1970) Tago Mago (1971) Ege Bamyasi (1972) Future Days (1973) Soon Over Babaluma (1974) Landed (1975) To this day I'm yet to see a rock band as consistent as CAN. There's a phrase for that: German precision.

What is the biggest lie society has taught you to believe? The 'strategy’ that worked for your parents will work for you. In Trinidad we have two different generations with two different mindsets. For ease of understanding I will label them: Any colonial Trinidadian will tell you that the older generation was far different from the modern non colonial, many will argue that, in terms of morals, norms and values, the Colonial mindset was better. The Colonials were greatly influenced by British standards. The path to one's success was deemed to be how closely he/she can emulate an upper class English person. Great emphasis was placed on education, speech (or the ability to speak the Queen's tongue without the influence of corruptive local dialect) and there was manic obsession of gaining recognition by ruling agents of our English masters through social acceptance (a combination of race and etiquette played a big role), scholarship, sport (mainly cricket) and if all else fails, kissing your parents goodbye and hopping aboard the HMT Windrush to the seek opportunity in the land of the Queen. Colonial parents were obsessed with their children's grades. Education was seen as the only means of upward mobility for those who had no other means of gaining English recognition. All of life seemed to be based around this rigid structure of class. The non-Colonials had little to no influence from the British. Those born after 1962 were privy to witness a near chaotic transition to self Government. Speaking proper English and demonstrating a level 'class’ now bore little to no impact on social mobility. Education and good grades provided some measure of success in life but was far less impactful than under British rule. Success was a combination of personal capitalistic drive and being 'in the know’ of certain opportunities the Government provided or exploits to be exploited. The US rather than the UK was now the chief model of success. Most of the laws the British provided were still in place but everyone from the the beggar on the street to the highest titled Government official approached them in 'read between the lines’ or 'you're only guilty if you're caught manner.’ The system is less rigid, less Draconian from the past, allowing, for better measures of opportunity for all levels of society but at the same time it operates within an opportunitistic, 'do as the Romans do,’ style bordering on controlled anarchy. As a boy I was drilled into believing that the path to success is getting good grades, speaking good English, maintaining a proper image, obeying the law and respecting elders. Now if I were to impart such wisdom to an average boy of this generation I would be scoffed at, not just by the boy, but also by his parents.

Were you popular in high school? Yes and no. In my early years I was just this odd kid with beaten up glasses who smiled a lot, was respectable to my elders but easily manipulated by my peers. I would constantly be prodded into starting fights with other weird kids and I would constantly lose those fights. Grating coconut and being caught eating it. I loved writing from an early age but had the mental temperament of a toddler even at ages 12–14. E.g. Elijah: Hey Melanie. Check out this new poem I wrote. Melanie: (Reads my love poem softly). Awww that's so sweet Elijah. Who's the lucky girl you going to give this to? Elijah: I'm giving it to you. I meant all that I wrote in it. Melanie: (blushes) But Elijah you know I have a boyfriend now. Elijah: What? I thought that was just a joke. How can he be your boyfriend? You only started taking to him a week or two ago. I've been friends with you since we started school. Melanie: Don't take it the wrong way. I like you too but he's older and more mature. Elijah: Yeah he looks old as hell. Melanie: Don't talk like that. Listen I just hope we can still be friends. Elijah: Friends! I'll show you friends. (Proceeds to tear up the poem in anger and walks away) I would then hang out with my group of loyal friends and we'd laugh manically at anything with an inkling of potential humour to stave off the pain and humiliation that we each got from our endeavours towards the opposite sex. From 15 and upwards I became a bit less awkward and a bit more refined. I discovered my tastes in music and while everyone grooved to Usher and Sean Paul I was becoming a self proclaimed hippie as I indulged in music from the 60s and 70s. Even though I stuck with my loyal, good-natured friends I began to learn and explore the different niches of kids my age. The popularity hierarchy went a bit like this. Top tier These were generally kids who had some measure of fame or infamy ; promiscuous kids, missing from school for long periods kids, the gang affiliated, football stars, the rich and not bashful about it, dating the hottest girl/boy in school and showing a lot of PDA kids, the consistently fashionable, defiant and challenging to authority kids etc etc. Middle tier Natural comedians, zany characters, stoners (high men as we called them), outspoken future politicians, natural businessmen, confident kids, gearheads, wildboys, good looking kids, athletic but not gifted kids, go-getters, nice guys and girls etc etc. Lower tier Shy kids, poverty stricken kids, teacher's pets, snitches, neurotics, overweight, ‘ugly’ kids, geeks, trying too hard kids etc etc. It's sad but that's how unwritten hierarchies was developed and it's still pretty much the same. School can be cruel. To be fair and honest, no one was guaranteed to remain in any one tier indefinitely. Shane, the most infamous bully of my class missed so much school that he was kept back a year and was sent to his younger brother's class under us. Shane went from top of the top tier to the absolute bottom in an instant. Siddhartha, was a unknown geek but went straight to the top when everyone found out he was the richest boy in school and he began flaunting it. I myself juggled between lower and middle throughout my high school tenure. Whenever I hung around the so-called top tier kids I honestly often felt something akin to sad desperation. They just seemed like miserable people who could never be themselves or had some serious hang ups in life. I didnt stick around them for long. Only when I came into adulthood doing my A’Levels did I become somewhat popular. I started to gain some measure of looks and an endless reserve of wit and confidence albeit with a significant lack of self discipline. I started mingling with everyone and in my cocky, self assurance I broke a few hearts and ended up having my own broken coming towards the end of high school. I think I was generally well liked and accepted amongst 80% of my peers and though I might have been a douche half the time, I was an entertaining, well-meaning and loyal douche throughout.

What are some inaccuracies or criticisms of JD Vance's book "Hillbilly Elegy"? Oh here we go again. So I'm supposed to assume this has nothing to do with the fact that Trump just appointed JD Vance as his running mate for Vice President. No. The person who asked the question is genuinely interested in a review of Vance's book and the question is in no way a negatively leading question. I haven't read the book yet but I saw the movie. I remember the movie was thrashed by critics and Hollywood acted as though Amy Adams should be drawn and quartered for taking part in such political, propagandist rubbish. The criticism was non stop. I almost believed what the media was saying. Then I watched it and was surprised to discover that it was a really good movie. It was just a simple story about a guy who struggled in life with poverty and drugs in his family and managed to make something of himself thanks to the two people who supported him in his life. The performances were excellent, particularly Amy Adams and Glenn Close and there was nothing remotely political or propagandist about the story. There is nothing in the book that merits me investigating the inaccuracies in the book. It is a memoir. Vance doesn't make any fantastic claims. It's not like Catch Me if You Can or My Wicked Wicked Ways. Did he exaggerate? Did his mother really overdose on heroin or was she just taking a nap? Is Vance's wife really of Indian descent or just three quarters Indian? Did Vance really drive all night to a job interview right after wrestling a heroin needle from his mother or did he just have a stern argument with her, took a nap and a plane the next morning? Does that matter? Are these the ‘inaccuracies’ that should make us condemn the book and Vance? It's astonishing how much the modern left have idealised themselves into believing that they are the final say in regards to everything. That they are never wrong. Any other opinions are stupid, racist or sexist. As a Trinidadian I sometimes argue with such people as to the reality of what goes on on in my country. People who've never even set foot in the country. When will they realize that the more arrogant they behave and the more they tell people what they ought to believe, think, say and feel, the more people will become disenchanted and start doing the opposite of what they suggest. I'm certain Vance's book and the film will see a surge in sales and streaming in the upcoming weeks. I might even come around to reading it, simply because so many critics angrily claim that I shouldn't.

What's the most obnoxious instance of America-centric behavior you've ever witnessed? During my first week at Papa John’s (Trinidad) the phone rang and I took the call. An American accent could be heard on the other end of the line. Caller: I’ll have the Friday special Me: Sorry ma’am but the specials are from Sundays - Wednesdays. Caller: This is Papa John’s right? Me: Yes. Caller: Papa John’s has Friday specials where I’m from. What’s the special for today? Me: Sorry but the specials are only from Sundays - Wednesdays. Caller: I’m goin’ write a review about the Papa John’s in Trinidad. I’ve traveled the world. I’ve never encountered any Papa John’s that doesn’t have a daily special. I want to talk to the manager. I call Ricardo, the manager, and he takes the phone. I’m expecting him to repeat what I said but instead he says ‘yes’ every few seconds and on the screen I see him enter two extra large pizzas, a large garlic bread sticks, a large cheese bread sticks and a 2L soda. He’s entering all these items, not as any discounted ‘special,’ but at retail value, so the bill is fairly sizable. He then covers the receiving end of the phone with his palm and tells me, ‘Go check and see if there’s any brownies left. I went in the chiller and saw two brownies remaining. I showed him two fingers and watch as he enters them both on the lady’s bill. He repeats the order to the caller. ‘So the total will be $502………no miss that is in Trinidad dollars. Yes miss that is a good deal you are getting…….OK…….Yes we take Mastercard………20 minutes…………thank you.’ He hung up the phone and looked at me smiling. ‘How did you manage to sell her all that stuff?’ I said, ‘She wanted a special.’ ‘I did give her a special,’ he says with a mischievous smile, ‘Ricardo’s special.’ He then proceeds to laugh flamboyantly and heads back to his office while saying, ‘Whenever you hear an American accent on the phone just call me…….I have a $10,000 sales target to make today.’

What are some of the biggest casting blunders in Hollywood movies? I know I may be in the minority with this opinion but when I saw that this guy would be cast as Peter Parker in the first major studio Spiderman movie, disappointment is not strong enough of a word to describe how I felt. Tobey Maguire does not have the wit, charisma and charm of a traditional Peter Parker. Not only that, Maguire was too old for the role from the very first movie. When I saw 27 year old Maguire walking about high school with a jacket, book bag and a distinct 5 o’clock shadow on his face I was immediately taken out of the movie. (Yeah that's definitely a teenaged schoolboy boarding a bus and not a smirking, semi-creepy man pushing 30) Peter Parker is a charming and witty young man, loyal to friends and family, a great problem solver and a smartass with a touch of geekiness. The only characteristic Tobey Maguire demonstrated from the above was the geekiness, of which he laid on as thick as cheesecake. Maguire’s Spiderman was this awkward, pitiable schmuck who had as much charisma and charm as a mild-mannered peeping tom. The whole shtick the producers seemed to go with was to make Peter Parker nothing but a sad, bullied nerd because I guess maybe they arrogantly believed Spiderman fans are nothing but a bunch of nerds who love the comic book not because of its quality story and characters but because it supports a geek fantasy of getting fantastic superpowers through simple means, getting to beat up thugs and bullies and winning chicks. Sam Raimi’s Spiderman targeted that niche when they gave us the whimpering, sensitive, thin-lipped Tobey Maguire as Peter Parker in my honest opinion. Maybe that's my personal opinion but personality aside, Maguire doesn't even have the physical attributes. Spiderman/Parker is 5′10, late teens-early 20s, lean, long-limbed, sinewy and with a head of thick brunette hair. He basically has to have the physique of a well experienced trapeze artist due to all the climbing and swinging Spiderman does. At his best in the film Tobey Maguire was a short limbed and somewhat stocky man measuring somewhere between 5′7 and 5′8 with a crop of thin hair above his smirking, punchable face. I grew up watching Spiderman cartoons and gaining a familiarity with Parker's smart, resonating and confident tone. Maguire's whiny, eerily pubescent voice gave a measure of cringe and creepiness. I am not a fan of Tobey Maguire's Peter Parker and will hold that view for the rest of my life. Andrew Garfield and Tom Holland may not be the gold standard either but they are a lot more closer to the mark. Here's hoping that they get it right the next movie.

What's the dumbest thing you've gotten in trouble for at school? Back in Form 2 (7th Grade) I fancied myself a comic book artist. To entertain myself and my friends I would draw these crude, intentionally homoerotic drawings of over muscled male wrestlers engaged in poses and grapples. My sense of anatomy and perspective was nothing short of abysmal so many of my drawings (at best) looked a lot like this. One of my friends asked that I draw our class teacher Mr. Din Chong. I made an atrocious rendering of him, exaggerating his physical features to a ludicrous degree and as an added touch I drew him shirtless and chicken Chester and pencil necked. The drawing looked nothing like him but my friends loved it and asked for more. I went home and drew the social studies teacher Ms. Moore (Big Shirley) as we called her, who was quite large and overweight. There was a running joke in the school that short, skinny big eared Din Chong and massive Big Shirley were a couple. I drew a comic showing Din Chong and Big Shirley going on a date and even had the nerve to draw explicit images of the two trying (unsuccessfully) to engage in sex. This comic was passed around the class with great fervor. Most of the class enjoyed my tasteless humour and even some of the bad boys were shocked that I went so far. Practically everyone told me to destroy the comic afterwards because something like that could get me in serious trouble if not suspended from school. However I had tasted some fame and was hungry for more. I started rendering practically all of the teachers in school in my dirty comic. I would include a lot of sex, a lot of violence (teachers we didn’t like being shot to pieces/decapitated by rasta gangsters. From just a few pages in my scrap book my comics grew to take up an entire note book. My comic book would be passed along in class whenever someone was bored and there would be a constant snorting and giggling and a declaration of shock from the reader. ‘You’re mad!’ one of the boys in class once told me, ‘One of the teachers are gonna find out about this.’ He then handed me back my notebook. I heard the warning so many times but I couldn’t care less. I had so many fans looking forward to a new panel of comics on a daily basis. Davan began to giggle like a 5 year old and I proceeded to continue onto my newest comic that involved a superhero with a massive dildo strapped to his head and his interaction with Big Shirley (much to Din Chong’s distress). After a minute or so I noticed there was no laughter coming from Davan. In fact, the class had grown eerily silent. Stupid me never considered the fact that my seat was next to a window and outside the window stood none other than the Principal peering down at me and my comic and listening rather broodingly, waiting for the moment when I realized that the shit had just hit the fan. I quickly closed the notebook and shoved it under my desk. ‘Let me see that’ she said. ‘It’s nothing’ I said ready to have a panic attack. ‘Boy. I said give me that book’ With a sense of impending doom I handed over the book to her. She flipped through the pages nonchalantly. I saw her eyes widen at some of the pages. ‘You are a very perverted young man’ she said stoically, ‘Follow me.’ Everyone stared as I followed the Principal to her office. It was rumored that she herself had a bit of a lewd sense of humour. Many of the boys on the football team would claim that she would drop a flirt or semi-sexual innuendo at their direction during after-school football practice. However, this comic involved practically every single teacher in the compound in a sexual and/or violent manner. This was nothing for her to joke about. I thanked the heavens that I never thought to include her in any of my comics. However, I was still deep in the shit and I could only imagine the look my mother would give me if she got to see these drawings. She told me to wait outside her office as she spoke to a teacher who had some sort of complaint. I was thinking she would say, ‘Hey, look at what this child did’ and hand him my drawings and pretty soon the whole staff room would come and see themselves rendered in the most atrocious manner and a big ruckus would start. Fortunately the teacher left unaware of the situation and the Principal then beckoned me in. The book was laid closed shut in her book shelf, looking innocent and inoffensive. ‘You have a great talent Mr. Williamson’ she said and stared at me. I didn’t know if to say thanks or smile so I remained silent. ‘You are also quite a disturbed boy and its very sad that you use your talents for such a negative purpose.’ Silence. She continued, ‘Let me catch you drawing more of these and I will make sure your parents are aware of what you do in your spare time. Is that understood?’ I nodded. I thought I was off the hook. What is the common parenting mistake and how can they rectify that? The worst parenting mistake is not showing any genuine love to your children. The most common parenting mistake ironically is to constantly be selflessly giving to them. I see it more as a source of vanity and pride rather than of genuine love. I have three relatives who are from such a household. Their parents are well-off and stable with the mother supplying them an abundance of love and the father an abundance of money whenever the time calls. All three of them are in their 40s and do not live in the same country as their parents. They come to see their parents every Christmas as a tradition. This sounds nice of them, for all three of them to arrange a date to arrive and stay at the family home, plane tickets etc. In reality their parents are the ones who see to that. The parents have been paying for their children to come see them for Christmas for over twenty years. The parents arrange the date, the tickets and additional expenses that their 40 something year old children may accrue during their stay. Some readers may not see a problem with this. If you can afford it, why not treat your kids, especially during the Christmas? My answer to them is that it has nothing to do with money. It has to do with principle. No one should have to pay to see their grown children once a year. If your kids really cared about you they would come on their own volition and expense, not wait for daddy to purchase highly inflated Christmas flights. Not only this but the parents (both in their 70s) are the one to pick them up upon arrival and drop them off for departure. The parents also provide them with a New Year's vacation to a hotel every year and pay all expenses associated with it. The parents cook meals, carry them out for lunch/dinner and arrange all forms of planning and entertainment. To say that their kids are somewhat spoiled would be quite an understatement. To say that their kids were concerned about their parents descent into old age, loss of movement/stamina and increasing loneliness would be a great exaggeration. This arrangement is likely to continue until one of their parents die of which I'm certain the other parent would have to buy their tickets so they can attend the funeral. When you train your kids that they can receive a constant supply of love without them having to reciprocate you are training them to expect love without having to reciprocate. This is almost as damaging as showing no love at all.

Do you think Europe is more racist than the USA? I haven't been to the whole of Europe and I haven't travelled all the States of the USA. However I've been to Wales and Kentucky recently and I've had two encounters that I think could be used as data towards answering the above question. Aberystwyth, Wales. I was a student on a scholar for a Masters degree along with a few fellow Trinidadians. When we went out shopping, our favourite store by far was Poundland. We patronized Poundland almost on a daily basis buying chocolates, sweets and various goodies for a pound each to our hearts’ delight. Despite the noticeable frigidity of many people in the area we saw, most were helpful and polite. One day at Poundland I was informed that there were rewards to anyone with purchases of over £25 pounds and up. The more you spent the better the reward. After shopping I checked my receipt and saw that I qualified to redeem a cool digital sports watch. I went over to the guy at customer service and showed my receipt. People from Aberystwyth tend to wear a constant smile that fluctuates from smile to smirk according to the mood/situation. This guy's smile changed to a definite smirk when he saw me waving my receipt. ‘What’s that you say?’ he said as though I were speaking Swahili. ‘I want to get the watch.’ I repeated for the third time, ‘I spent over thirty pounds.’ He watched me waving my receipt with a confused expression on his face as though I were a lunatic waving a bill of rights. ‘Come again?’ he said and I knew he was playing stupid and I started to get annoyed. I notice that he's glancing towards the back of the store as if to communicate to the others that he wanted someone else to come over. Suddenly an older man came towards us and asked what was the problem. I explained that I wanted to redeem my points for the sports watch. I showed him the receipt but he stares at me up and down instead. ‘You’re not from the UK I would guess,’ he says. I said no, that I was here on studies. He hemmed and hawed and then said that the prizes are meant for UK citizens. I told him that there was no mention of that in the advertisement hanging on the wall next to him. He hemmed and hawed again and said that it may not be written in the ad but the promotion is to encourage locals to shop at Poundland more. I asked to speak to the manager and with a smirk he said, ‘Nice to meet you. I'm the manager Steve.’ Him and the other worker then proceeded to stare at me, brandishing their wide smile-smirks. Deciding not to make a ruckus I left the matter at that. Georgetown, Kentucky I visited my girlfriend and we stopped at the police station at the above location for her to deal with a matter. While I was waiting for her in the car I grew bored after 30 minutes. There was a swarm of bees that surrounded the area and as they left I went out to take a video of them as the swarmed off. A police car rolls up about 20 feet away from me and the driver's window rolls down. A latino officer then smiles at me and says ‘Hey.’ I said Hi. He says something else but I couldn't hear him so I went closer to his vehicle. He asks me what I was doing there in the car park and I explained that I was waiting for a friend inside the station. He asked me where I was from and I explained that I was from the Caribbean. Suddenly another police car comes speedily from the opposite direction and parks in an aggressive manner as if to cut me off from running away. A tall stocky Caucasian officer exits the vehicle and comes towards me and demands that I keep my hands away from my pockets. He proceeds to search me and discovers me unarmed. He explains that someone reported me as a suspicious individual hanging around the police station parking lot. I explained that I was just a tourist from the Caribbean. They explained that loitering about a police station is seen as suspicious in the State of Kentucky and that I should remain in my vehicle if I waited on my friend here. Tall stocky guy stares at me and asks if I have any questions myself. I said no but I said I appreciated how alert they were and if only Trinidad had such dedicated officers we would have less crime. They both laugh awkwardly and stocky guy pats me on my shoulder like a schoolkid. They both leave without another word. In conclusion I would honestly say that my experience in Wales seemed to border more on seething racism rather my experience in Kentucky. I believe the officers in Georgetown were doing their job whilst the staff at Poundland at Aberystwyth were discriminating in a subtle manner. There was a certain deep seated resentment I felt in Wales whilst in Kentucky it was more of a passive wariness. I felt as though I could've communicated to the officers and reach a certain compromise whilst with the Poundland staff I felt like a brick wall was between us. I also felt like that with the locals of Kentucky, a friendly warmth while in Aberystwyth it was an air of cold professionalism for the most part. In rural Kentucky, places like Kuttawa and Paducah I got no strange looks and witnessed black people working alongside whites in seeming normalcy whereas in Aberystwyth the one black person I witnessed was a homeless man and the one mixed race person was young man working in a thrift shop. So in my honest and ignorant opinion I would think that racism would be more prevalent in a subtle, passive aggressive manner in Europe whilst in the US it can happen due to wariness of strangers rather than due to race. Edit: There is one commenter who continuously alleges that I’ve fabricated my story about my visit to Wales and Aberystwyth. Every time I reply with evidence to him it somehow disappears so I’ve decided to put the evidence where it can’t be removed here in the answer.

Who is the most underestimated horror movie villain? Practically every boy who grew up in the 90s watching horror movies on SyFy (then Sci-Fi) knew of this guy. I'm pretty certain he's responsible for a lot of nightmares we had back then. Revok from David Cronenberg’s sci-fi/body-horror cult classic Scanners (1981) puts a capital V in Villain. He's a powerful, ruthless and deranged psychic (scanner) bent on taking over the world with powers that can control minds and inflict severe physical damage on others. Michael Ironside who portrays Revok is nothing short of excellence. He makes Jack Nicholson’s Joker look like Mr. Rogers with his intense facial expressions, sinister grimacing and lip curling as well as his menacingly emotionless voice. No one can forget the famous scene at the beginning of the movie where Revok calmly and sarcastically pretends to be ‘scanned’ by a weaker fellow scanner only to casually cause the man's head to explode within seconds. Few actors can put such a stamp on a performance like Ironside did as he did with Revok. Scanners may be a bit of a forgotten movie by now but no one can ever forget the character Revok and Ironside's performance.

What was the kindest thing someone did for you when you were young? I was a bit of a scatterbrain as a 10 year old. I used to have after-school lessons that would last until 4pm. One evening, after lessons, I checked my wallet and noticed that my traveling money was missing. Being the bright young lad that I was I calculated that since my home was an hour's drive away, I could walk home and it would only take me 2–3 hours at most. I didn't factor in my calculations that my home was an hour's drive away on the highway. I used to watch a lot of adventure cartoons where the hero treks through forests and vast plains for days on end. I told myself that it would be an adventure just like the cartoons. Fast forward three hours later and I'm only a little after the halfway mark. The sun had long set and I'm about to enter the infamous Cleaver Woods (which was, back then, used by murderers to dump bodies). I'm completely exhausted to the point of laying on the ground crying. Suddenly a tall man in his mid to late 20s calls over to me in a voice in which I immediately sense that belonged to a friendly, humourous type person. 'I was liming (hanging out) with my friends in Curepe and I saw you walking. I went to Arouca and I saw you walking. Now I'm home and I see you're still walking...’ I explained the situation and he began to laugh. 'You're mad,' he said, 'Why didn't you take the bus? It's free for school children.’ I felt like a dope. Indeed I had some bus tickets remaining in my wallet and several buses did pass while I was walking. He went to a shop and returned with a snack and a drink for me. While I ate and drank he told me about the dangers of Cleaver Woods and how I could get killed walking through there at night. He then gave me $10 to get a taxi home. He stayed with me until I was put in a taxi and when I was seated and secured he waved goodbye and left. I was so exhausted I don't believe I even told him thank you or asked his name. He didn't seem to care. It looked like what he just did was something normal for him on a day to day basis. At the time the only thing I thought was nice what he did was how he spent money on me. As I grew older I realized that it was much more than that. He looked out for me. Instead of focusing on his own affairs he narrowed his concentration on me and pondered to my ordeal and my safety and made it his duty to help this random boy who had nothing to do with him. At the time my father was absent from my life. This was my first father figure encounter and I could never forget him and what he did.

I'm a school custodian and when people ask me what's my job I'm ashamed to tell them. What's the best way I could say what I do without saying I'm a custodian? Embrace the fact that you are a janitor. Yes. I said it. A janitor. You work for a living. You work hard. You are valuable salt of the Earth. People feel comfortable around you and feel more at ease to talk to you because you hold no airs about yourself. People admire you because you do a job that most people don't want and when you do it with pride you are an inspiration. I'm sure if you tell the staff around you your plans to get a degree or invest in a small business you will get an overwhelming amount of support. Everyone loves to see the little guy make small steps. No one likes to hear the big rich CEO gushing about a planned merger or a thriving stock portfolio. No. People love to hear about the janitor who saved his money and started his own cleaning company. You also have the benefit of always knowing who are your real friends. Lawyers, doctors and politicians don't have that benefit. Everyone is running to kiss their ass and use them. Nobody is running to kiss Larry the janitor’s ass and use him. You know that people who don't respect you or your work, no matter how well you perform it, are people to stay away from. You don't have to have your back against the wall to see your enemies. Be proud of who you are. You work hard. Not many people do that. And if anyone asks what you do for a living say with pride that you are a school janitor. Their reaction will say a lot about them Written by a former delivery ‘boy.’

Why is a bronze medal winner happier than a silver medal winner? What is counterfactual thinking? Imagine Jimmy watching the lottery results live on television. 30 (Nice) 23 (Heyy!) 6 (Heyyyy!) 5 (Oh my God!) 8 (Oh my ****** God!) Jumps off couch And the final number… 33 (Nooooooooo. 33! Who the **** plays 33? It's 27. No. No.No.) Falls back onto the couch sobbing. Jimmy got 5 out of the 6 numbers correct. He is rewarded with one tenth of the grand cash prize. Jimmy is heartbroken. All his life he's waited for that moment. All his life he's played the National Lottery dreaming of the day. It was supposed to be today. He feels as though he wants to die. Better he had gotten zilch and saved himself this torment. Freddie is on his security shift. He hears on the radio that one person has won the grand prize. Some people have all the luck. He remembers he bought a ticket and checks to see if he scraped anything. He’s astonished to see that he got 4 out of 6 numbers correct. He got an entire year's salary through sheer luck. He is overjoyed. Far more overjoyed than Jimmy who got ten times his winnings. Moral of the story is that second place winners tend to feel overwhelming disappointment that they were so close to winning while third place winners tend to be happy that they at least got something.

What is the smallest scam you have ever seen? Back in 2003 I was a bit of a wacky, teenaged schoolboy. Heading home, I chanced upon a short, scruffy looking man selling a sad collection of pirated DVDs in front of the bank. I say sad because he didnt even have a proper DVD stand nor did he have those neat colored computer printed DVD jackets. No. He held in his hand a collection of cheap, brandless DVD-R discs upon which he scribbled in his unpleasant handwriting, random movie titles such as Love Don't Cost A Thing and National Security. I paid him no heed but then I heard him call to me, ‘Yo, yo check out what I got youth-man.’ I shook my head in refusal and continued past him until he spoke again. ‘Bank Girls Gone Wild my youth,’ he whispered loudly, ‘…local Trini girls.’ My ears pricked up. I went straight up to him. ‘You mean local girls naked?’ I whispered, ‘Naked? That is joke. These girls not just naked my youth……real rudeness.` ‘Bank girls? Even the girls from this bank?’ I said pointing at the bank behind him. At this point I was really excited. Such things were unheard of in our mostly conservative society. Also I was really attracted to one particular young woman who worked at the very bank he stood in front of. ‘Yeah’ he replied and showed me a DVD with no writing on it, ‘This here is bank girls from up north and central. You will see your girl on this DVD. I have bank girls from down south too.’ I was already sold at that point but something made me suspicious. ‘How come you didn't label this DVD? You sure it’s the right one you giving me?’ He was silent for a second then he replied, ‘You want me to get locked up? I can't go around showing everybody I selling Bank Girls Gone Wild…This is real black market business my youth.. So what you say? It's $25 for the DVD, over 3hrs of footage. I`ll give you this one together with the Bank Girls: Down South Edition for $40.’ I was expecting him to sell such a rare item for at least $100. It was a steal of a deal. I told him I just wanted the North-Central Girls DVD. I paid him his money and went home excitedly. No one was home so I immediately stuck the DVD in the player and waited. As the reader would've probably guessed by now, the DVD was a blank. I was scammed. I paid $25 for a generic blank DVD worth $7 max at retail value. I thought the guy would've been smart enough to take his scam to a different location but a few days afterwards I spotted him in front of the bank again, with his same DVD shtick. I went up to him. ‘Mister,’ I said angrily, ‘Gimme back my money or I'm going to the police.’ ‘Whoa youth man,’ he said in a surprisingly calm voice, ‘What is it with the bad vibes?` ‘You sell me a blank DVD. I want back my $25.’ ‘You sure it blank? You sure is not your DVD player not working?` He spoke so calmly and was so unintimidated with his confused and guiltless manner. I started to wonder if maybe I was wrong. Being a horny teenager who really wanted to see these nude bank girls didnt help my situation either. ‘Hear what,’ he continued, ‘I probably gave you the wrong DVD. I probably gave you a blank by mistake.’ He then pulled out a DVD that bore a B&W jacket showing a topless woman captioned Bank Girls Gone Wild: Director's Cut. If I had a tail like a dog, it would've been wagging. I was incredibly excited. ‘Take this copy and when you get chance, bring back my blank DVD for me.’ ‘Thank you,’ I cried while shaking his grubby hands excitedly. I went home and waited until late in the night while my family slept. I stuck in the DVD with more nervous anticipation than a defenseless goalkeeper seeing a star forward thundering towards him. BLANK DVD He did it go me again. However I couldnt help but laugh. He plotted his petty scam better than a Magnus Carlsen endgame. I had to be the biggest idiot on Earth, but it served me right. I never saw that guy again. He was smart enough to carry his scam to a different location. Edit 21.01.22. Ever had someone 'molest’ your food. What are the wrong depictions of the US in Hollywood movies? When I think of a Hollywood movie that is far removed from any possible spectrum of realism, this movie always comes to my mind. You can tell by just watching the poster that this is going to be another formulaic family movie; the white background which signifies that this movie will have no content, dialogue or subplot other than this generic couple and their darned dog, the smiling figures staring at you almost sinisterly, the tepid humour of a puppy leading the couple by leash. “A dog leading its masters by leash?…….. that's so clever and ironic!” Sarcasms and cynicisms aside, here are the reasons why this movie is not just a wrong depiction of US life but an offense to ordinary people who tighten their belt and blue collar while slaving it on the 9 to 5. 1. Raising a dog = good practice for raising children, according to this movie. The above image perfectly captures how stupid that notion is. No one would watch a photo like this and and say that this is evidence of good parental skills. Besides feeding and caring there is nothing remotely similar to raising dogs as compared to children. This is a notion you tend to see solely in Hollywood movies where raising children can be condescended to the same level as keeping a litter of puppies. Raising good children, especially for poorer parents, is practically a lifelong sacrifice and the ultimate moral contract. Giving up your youth, freedom and finances and being willing to shield your child from incoming physical harm or even death is not the same as a bowl of Kibbles n Bits and a scratch on the tummy. 2. Every middle class American lives in a mansion on a sprawling well-kept spread of land. Owen Wilson and Jennifer Aniston's characters are ordinary reporters with two kids. She becomes a stay at home mom which makes him the breadwinner. His highest paying position is at The Philadelphia Inquirer which, according to online research, currently has an average annual salary of $60,000. This would mean that his monthly salary would've been around $5000 give or take. This 16 acre five bedroom Pennsylvania farmhouse had a selling price of $1.25 million in 2011. Using a mortgage calculator based on local interest rates at the time his payment for the house would’ve been roughly $5800 per month based on a 30 year loan repayment. So in other words, for the family to have realistically lived such a lifestyle, Jennifer Aniston's character had to have employed some means of soliciting tax-free money at night. 3. Let's all shed tears……. A dog has died of old age. This was the moment that was the straw that broke the camel's back. We ejected the DVD in sheer annoyance and frustration at this point. The dog died……a natural death. Cue sad music and flashbacks. How entitled can your country be if the natural death of a dog can elicit tears from an audience? A pet dog in Trinidad is lucky to live past 8 years, even in the best of care. My own backyard where I grew up contains the remains of over a dozen unfortunate cats and canines who died prematurely due to illness, speeding cars and just plain bad luck. We had not a single pet that died of natural causes i.e. old age. If we did, we would have celebrated its life and the fact that it led a full life. This supposed tearjerking scene was just another alienating Hollywoodism that highlights how out of touch the film industry is. What an awful movie full of delusional perceptions of the average American life. Don't watch it.

What movie felt like you were right there with the actors? United 93 Didn't have the opportunity to see this on the big screen when it premiered back in ‘06. Really wish I did. However I'm certain I would've been emotionally drained afterwards. The film deals with the September 11th terrorist attacks and chronicles the last few hours of the only flight of the four hijacked planes in which the passengers managed to fight off the terrorists and prevent the plane from crashing into its intended target. The film employs the use of shaky, handheld camera which has become the signature style of its director Paul Greengrass (of whom I am of the opinion that he now overdoes this style in practically every movie he makes). The frenzied handheld style coupled with the use of real time, unknown actors, strategic camera positioning and lack of a protagonist makes the viewer feel like a random passenger aboard the flight. All of this is done intentionally by the director of course. It is one of the few movies in which, even though I knew what would be the eventual outcome, I was glued to the screen in nervous anticipation as to what was going to happen next. A very underrated movie in my honest opinion.

What are some dirty tactics used by fast food restaurants? I worked delivery for a popular local pizzeria in Trinidad for some years and left somewhat dishonorably discharged after having arguments with management over a growing reliance on a dirty, illegal tactic that they employed with no discretion. I can best describe it by means of a short skit. Customer: Hi. Good day. Do you have any specials today? Newly Employed Cashier: Good day. Our Monday special is two large pizzas for only $100. Customer: That's great. That's like two for the price of one. I'll have it. Newly Employed Cashier: Yes. We have a different specials everyday. You can check them online or simply ask us. Customer: I appreciate. Great service. The Manager is in the background keenly observing the proceedings. After the customer leaves she approaches the cashier. Manager: Did you just sell that man two pizzas for $100? Newly Employed Cashier: Uh...yeah...the special? Manager: So you sold just the two pizza special? What about the donuts and cookies that we’ll have to discard this evening? What about the salad? I need you to sell all of these before the end of the day. Newly Employed Cashier: I'm trying but most people just want the two pizzas for $100 special. Manager: This branch doesn’t have a two pizzas for $100 special. Our special is two pizzas, four donuts, four cookies and a salad for $160. Newly Employed Cashier: But that's not what we have advertised. What if….. Manager: What if we have this discussion about this in Head Office tomorrow? A new customer walks in with his wife and two children and approaches the cashier. Customer 2: Hi. I heard you guys have some kind of special for two pizzas? The cashier glances at the Manager staring at her. Newly Employed Cashier: Yes. Two pizzas, four donuts, four cookies and a salad for $160. Customer 2: Okay. I really don't want all that other stuff. I could've sworn I saw online it was just two pizzas for the price of one….? He stares intently at the cashier and hoping for her to give him the offer he wanted. His wife then urges him to take the offer as the kids are getting restless. The customer grudgingly accepts. The customer behind him is well dressed in a suit and is discussing a legal matter with a client on his cell phone. Customer 3: Hi. I'll have the two pizza special. One pepperoni, the other veggie. Newly Employed Cashier: The special today is two pizzas with four donuts… She feels a nudge on her arm. The Manager is motioning for her to shut up. What are some plot holes in some of famous movies? Recently rewatched the 2009 Star Trek film. Don't get me wrong I absolutely love this movie. I think by a long shot it is the greatest reimagining of a popular series and one of the greatest sci-fi adventures of the 21st century. However this part of the plot sticks out like a sore thumb for me. Nero, an angry and embittered Romulan from the future enacts revenge on Spock and his Vulcan race for not being able to save his planet Romulus. With his massive ship he drills a hole into the core of planet Vulcan and inserts ‘red matter’ into the core. This creates a black hole that absorbs the planet committing genocide upon the 6 billion inhabitant Vulcan race (apart from Spock, his father and a few ‘elders’). This grim aspect of the plot takes the normally light-hearted Star Trek to a whole new level of ‘shit just got serious’ seriousness. However, something about these Vulcans just don't add up. The Planet Vulcan Spock and the Vulcan race are supposed to be one of the most intelligent race of beings in the galaxy. One of their biggest traits is to maintain logic over emotion at all times. They store and process information at a volume and speed exponentially greater than humans, they are adept at learning and transmitting knowledge and their analytical skills and foresight would make living Chess legend Magnus Carlsen look like a baboon playing with his toy. Yet look at where they live. This shithole is planet Vulcan. As you can see it is a wasteland full of rocks and sand. As brilliant as these Vulcans are, their architecture looks like a bombed out Cairo at best. Vulcans are humanoid. They need food, water and sex to procreate. They admire beauty, they fall in love and they have something of a sense of humour. Their planet looks to be 20% water within a huge, dry continent devoid of vegetation of any sort. How did their population manage to reach six billion living on a hot, arid and infertile planet? Why did they never decided to colonize a more agreeable and unoccupied planet? I'm pretty sure the Federation would allow it. If they are so advanced in technology why can't they properly develop their planet and find means of increasing and distributing their water supply or getting some trees to grow? Are the Vulcan's really that smart? The Vulcans have the ability to create black holes at an instant yet they have zero defense against Romulan ships blasting holes deep into the core of their planet. They have no planetary shield, no defense satellite, no space army, they don't even have ships to escort their people off the planet. They depend entirely on Starfleet to repel the enemy and evacuate the people. Yet we're supposed to believe them to be creatures of the highest logic. The Vulcans have sent a distress call to Starfleet about their planet being attacked. I'm guessing the distress call was a bit like this: ‘Hey bros send help. Some idiot is drilling a hole into our crappy planet. It's making a lot of noise and really annoying.’ ‘Hey sorry. Forgot to warn you that they have a massive ship, 50 times bigger than the biggest Starfleet warship and using technology and weaponry that is so powerful that it most likely comes from the future. ‘Hope you sent warships and the Starfleet army and not just your student trainees and scout ships…..you did! Crap.’ ‘We’ll just go offer our prayers to our giant stone idols in our primitive church cave where you can't get a signal to beam us to safety.’ ‘If anything just send Spock to come get us.’ That aspect of the film is so utterly ludicrous that it takes me out of the movie a tad bit. Great movie nonetheless.

What do fast food employees think of customers who come in frequently, say, multiple times a week or even daily? Thank you, whomsoever asked this beautiful question. Working as a delivery rider for a popular pizza restaurant it was fascinating how the regular customers seemed to be at polar extremes. There was hardly a middle ground. The regulars were either exceedingly pleasant i.e. the ever smiling, courteous customer who knew you by name, empathized with you, were patient and just radiated warmth and kindness. I would refer to them as the sweethearts. Or there were the ones who saw fast food personnel as a cheap means to vent their personal frustrations, felt entitled (because they believed the company would not survive without them), always tried to 'beat the system,’ always cheap, petty and discourteous and always naturally doing something aggravating to everyone around them e.g. taking up two parking spaces, refusing to sit and wait for the order (standing impatiently by the cashier with folded arms and sullen face) and giving details as to all the operational flaws they've witnessed with the restaurant whilst preaching how they would fix these flaws if they owned the restaurant. I would refer to these as the soul-eaters. Unfortunately I can only distinctly remember the experiences with soul-eaters. Here are three fascinating accounts. The Coffee Boys. Every Saturday night a group of preppy young men, all between the ages of 18 — 20 would come to the restaurant. There were usually five of them and they would occupy an entire table. They would sit at this table for more than an hour regardless if they had long finished their meal, denying that space for other diners. What was the meal they each ordered that merited leasing the table for such an extended period of time: One cup of coffee. That didn't bother any of us. It's not our restaurant, the company has no policy against such an obvious loss-incurring action and we were trained that the customer is always right. What made them unlikable was how they went about ordering their single cup of coffee. The ringleader, the most preppy of them all, would do the ordering. Despite being just some 18yo kid just off of cricket practice, he would speak to you as though he's the son of the owner of the restaurant. 'Things are pretty slow for the hour huh…..Susan?’ 'Patrice…… Are those cookies fresh or are they from the morning batch?’ 'Looks like you need a new shirt huh…… Phillip?’ He would always call out your name from your name tag, not as a show of courtesy, but in an authoritative almost passive-aggressive manner. After a minute or two of his condescending conversation, he would request 5 coffees with cream, literally the cheapest item on the menu. The cashier would pour them out in cups, neatly cover them with lids and place them on a tray. The words 'thank you’ or even subtle gesture of appreciation would never emanate from him as he would eye the cups, lift a cup to his face, remove a lid, sniff at coffee and take a sip in a manner as though he is the ultimate connoisseur of generic fast food coffee. 'Ummm. Maria?’ he would say to the cashier after taking his sip. The cashier would nod and come to him. He would then continue, 'Something is up with this coffee…I think you need to check your coffee machine.’ Then a hullabaloo would ensue with different members of staff tasting the coffee, not finding anything wrong. The manager would come out and taste the coffee and find no fault with it. However coffee-boy is not satisfied until he sees the coffee machine opened up to reveal that there is indeed sufficient powdered coffee and creamer in the machine. The five original cups of coffee are discarded and the cashier has to keep adjusting the machine and pouring out coffee, giving coffee-boy a sample to taste until he finds it is just right. Five fresh cups of coffee are then poured and he goes to his gang to occupy the table for over an hour after having caused over $50 worth of wasted coffee and cups. The Church Group. Once a month, on a Sunday night a large group of people who just finished worshiping at a nearby church would come into the restaurant. Their orders would be large, usually ranging between 4 — 6 family sized pizzas. They were courteous, patient and would attempt to be friendly. However they never failed to infuriate us all whenever they came. Firstly they would always come just a few minutes before closing time to place a big order. Though they could've easily called pick up an hour in advance, they preferred to come when we've already washed up the dishes and mopped the floor, anxiously waiting the closing time. 'I'm sorry but we've closed off dining for the night as we are about to close. You could only have the order as a take-away.’ the cashier would tell them. 'Oh well,' the pastor of the group would say, 'Well then we'll have to forget about the order.’ He's saying this but he knows that we cannot refuse a large order no matter how near it is to closing time. He knew that if the head office got wind of our branch refusing a $500+ order, we would be reprimanded. He knows all this but he is pretending to show humility for his church congregation. The cashier would acquiesce and remind the pastor that in ten minutes time we would be closing. The pastor would smile and assure the cashier that they wouldn’t be long. Staff would have to reheat the ovens, gather all the dough and ingredients that were neatly packed away in the chillers and grudgingly prepare these pizzas, knowing fully well that the order would be finished beyond our closing hour, after which we would have to wait for the church group to finish their meal. The restaurant would close at 10 pm on a Sunday. The church group would get their meal at around that time. Even though we’ve already tucked away the chairs and neatly aligned the tables for the next day, the church group would drag about a couple tables and join them together. Anything that is request-able you bet your bottom the group would request it; more napkins, more cups with ice, more condiments, turn off the air condition please, OK its too warm now, can you turn it back on, mini boxes to carry home leftovers, plastic bags, can this pizza be warmed over? etc, etc. While they are eating, the pastor, though he knows that he promised he will not stay long is encouraging members of the group to share tame, inoffensive church-based jokes and stories. All of us would and listen as Mrs. Nora recounted the time when she sent her grandson to get Communion bread but he didn't remind her that he wasn't a confirmed Catholic yet; how she gave him a good licking that evening when they returned home. The pastor howled with laughter. We would then interrupt their laughter to explain to them that we were ready to lock the building. The pastor would act surprised and apologize for losing track of time. We would wait another 10 minutes as they scrambled to distribute leftovers and gather their belongings. They wouldn’t even bother to help tidy back the area because they are now suddenly concerned about overstaying their time. They all apologized and thanked us for being so patient with them. We would then have to clean up all their spills, stains, used napkins, cups, pizza boxes and trays, re-wipe the tables, re-mop the floor and reposition the tables and chairs. We would lock the restaurant and when we exited the building the church group would be outside hanging about near their vehicles, continuing their conversation. Most of us didn’t have vehicles and would struggle that late hour to get a taxi as the streets would be near-deserted. None of the church group members would even consider offering us a ride as they left the restaurant in their cars. The Pool Guy. Lastly, there was a guy who would come in every day after work to place the same order of a mini pizza with chicken. I can’t remember his name but he would always mention to whomsoever was cashing that he was ‘building his pool.’ That pool must’ve been deeper than the Atlantic Ocean because for years he would always mention that pool that he was building. I can say without the slightest doubt that pool-guy was an asshole. I’m not even going to try to be subtle about it. He was a certified piece of s**t. Of all the scummiest people I’ve met on this Earth, he ranks in the top 5. Pool guy was a short hairy guy in his mid to late 30’s with a head full of graying hair. He always had a disheveled, resentful look as though he just woke up from a sleepless night with a terrible hangover. He was always making threats, harassing or trying to intimidate the mostly female workers to get some sort of preferential treatment i.e. being served before everyone else, getting more toppings on his pizza etc. Such tactics were common on an everyday basis but what set pool guy apart was that he naturally wanted to piss you off and provoke you to the limits of what is legally allowed. Pool guy definitely had some personal problems in his life and saw the restaurant as a means to vent his anger and frustration. Pool guy seemed as though he couldn’t overcome certain obstacles/people in his life so instead he would channel this anger into abusing a bunch of hapless, minimum wage earning women in a fast food restaurant. His tactic was that he would enter the restaurant and with no common courtesy he would gruffly order his mini pizza with chicken. He would remind the cashier at what time he placed his order and would subtly threaten that waiting makes him angry and we really don’t want to see him when he’s angry. He would then stand with arms folded, hearing distance away from the cashier, refusing to take his seat until he got his order. Most of us knew that he didn’t really care about the order. He got his thrill in harassing and psychologically abusing the more timid female staff at the front counter. ‘Go check on my order,’ he would demand every couple of minutes, ‘I’m waiting too long.’ Nothing thrilled him more than when his order took longer than the standard 15 minutes. Now he had an excuse to abuse. ‘Where is my order?’ he would shout. If no one answered him he would use this as an excuse to become vile. ‘ Like there’s only stupid, slow and uneducated people working in here?’ or ‘If I was your ‘child-father’ (baby-daddy) you would’ve moved faster.’ or ‘You could be a disappointment to your family but don’t disappoint me here today.’ The most pathetic thing about pool guy was that he would never dare behave like that in the presence of other customers. He would step away when a queue of customers were around and when they dispersed, like a rat coming out of his hole he would return to provoke and insult. There was never a single moment where he displayed a likable side to him. When he was in a good mood, he wouldn’t threaten and abuse but he would instead rant about his achievements in life. He claimed that he owned a fleet of trucks and his family were of great wealth and status that they practically owned the entire North coast of Trinidad. He would talk about how he traded in his cars every five years, that he spent over 5 million on his house in the past three years and how he was thinking of widening the pool that he had under construction and choosing a different set of tiles than what he originally intended I never met another delivery rider who didn’t feel like punching pool guy’s face in after being forced to listen to one of these boastful and selfish conversations. Funny enough, we got word that his niece was to be employed at the restaurant. The day she arrived at the restaurant pool guy mysteriously stopped coming. His niece explained to us that he was the most detested member of the family. He did not own a fleet of trucks but rather worked loading goods on and off a truck for a major cosmetics retailer. Also, he lived, not in a $5 million dollar+ house but in a tiny annex at his parents’ house which was next to her parents. By no means did the family own any property at the North coast let alone the entire North Coast. We asked if he had a pool and to our surprise she said yes, his family did indeed have a pool. Which extremely surreal film would you consider to be worth watching? The most fascinating surreal film I have ever seen has to be Fellini Satyricon (1969). Did I say most fascinating, surreal movie? I think I could go on a limb and say the most fascinating movie I’ve ever seen is Fellini Satyricon (1969). The movie should’ve been called Fellini Paradox or Fellini Irony . The movie makes absolutely no sense……yet it is understandable. The movie is stunningly gorgeous yet repulsive. It celebrates love and camaraderie yet blanketed in lust, hatred, envy and deception. It can be as richly interwoven as 1001 Arabian Nights, as profound as Shakespeare yet vulgar enough to make the Marquis de Sade proud. Encolpius and Ascyltus are strikingly handsome students in Ancient Rome. They both vie for the affection of Giton, an androgynous, underage male concubine of sorts. Their pursuit of Giton’s affections leads them to a dream-like odyssey involving pirates, hedonists, blood thirsty mercenaries, hermaphrodite demi-gods, minotaurs, women with flaming vaginas, sorcerers, impostor Caesars and the like. The story progresses in a somewhat fragmented nature due to the missing texts of the author Petronius. This can be jarring at first view but upon repeated viewing it adds to the enigma. However the most fascinating aspect of the movie is the production design by Danilo Donati. Despite whatever inherent historical inaccuracies, no film comes remotely close to this film in terms of costume, set design and just plain old aesthetics. This is definitely a love it or passionately detest it movie. However no one can deny its power to shock and awe.

Would Hollywood actor Brad Pitt have made it in old or classic Hollywood back in the day? Very interesting question. For the sake of simplification let's just assume that by Classic Hollywood you mean the Hays Code era of Hollywood whereas sex, nudity, graphic violence, rape etc could not be demonstrated in Hollywood films. (1934 — 1968) 1930s — 1940s Hollywood Hollywood in the aftermath of the Great Depression and the outbreak of the Second World War. This is the age of the Go-Getter and although silent movies are now obsolete, it's exaggerative stage acting style is still rampant. Audiences of this era are favorable towards a certain type of male screen presence. Popular actors of the era are mostly an embodiment of what were considered desirable, manly traits. This is the era of Clark Gable, Cary Grant, Gary Cooper, James Stewart, Errol Flynn, John Wayne and Henry Fonda. The archetypal male film star was usually tall (over 6 feet), athletic, handsome, possessing a rich and resonant voice and possessing a certain self assured alpha male quality. The kind of man who would've made a great career as a top salesman or workforce motivator. The nation was wounded after two World Wars and these idealistic tropes were coveted by men and women alike. It was an age that was obsessively preoccupied with courage, persistence and survival. It was the era of sucking in your emotions and holding your chin high. Unless in possession of exemplary acting skills or song and dance expertise, actors who lacked several of these traits were relegated to minor supporting roles, comic relief roles, extras, stunt work or failed to make it in the film industry at all. Despite being ruggedly handsome, Brad Pitt would've had a hard time getting work in Hollywood during this era. He did not fit the height requirement, his voice would not be considered rich and animated and his brooding, sombre presence would've been a turn off for a national audience hungry for the next cocky, high shouldered, go-getting macho man. 1950s Hollywood The ideal aforementioned leading man is still prevalent with Charlton Heston, Gregory Peck, Burt Lancaster, and Rock Hudson maintaining the status quo. However standards are less rigid as actors like William Holden, Frank Sinatra, Kirk Douglas, Yul Brynner and Tony Curtis, who have the macho appeal but lack the height, are some of the top stars. A growing interest in brooding more sensitive type 'method' acting is gaining ground with the likes of James Dean, Marlon Brando and Paul Newman. Brad Pitt would've been better able to find work in such type roles but the competition would be fierce and only those with extensive stage experience and schooled in New York at the Actor's Studio would get top priority over some quiet, good looking guy from Missouri. 1960s Hollywood The growing counterculture revolution is finally making an impact on Hollywood. While the war scarred older generation is fading to make way for the Baby Boomers, the conservative values and ideal macho leading man is no longer as appealing for those hungry for emotional catharsis. The audience is yearning for a leading man who they could relate to, who shares their flaws and can demonstrate vulnerability. Even the more macho type actors are expected to demonstate weakness and more sensitivity. These would include Clint Eastwood, Sean Connery, Charles Bronson, Steve McQueen, Robert Redford, George Kennedy and Rod Steiger. Slurred speaking (Marlon Brando), meek voiced (Eastwood) overweight (Steiger) and short stature (Bronson) are traits no longer shunned by Hollywood elite. Brad Pitt would've found the greatest chance of obtaining prominent roles during this era. Who knows he might've even replaced Robert Redford in Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid.

What was the first thing you saw, heard or discovered that made you feel old? I was working as a delivery rider for Pizza Hut back in 2015. I was at a rather difficult stage in my life, strapped for cash, domestic problems and an admitted depleted sense of self worth. However I always prided myself on my youthful exuberance. I believed I could’ve pass for 23 even though I was a few months shy of 30. I stopped to deliver at a small grocery. It was late at night and I was fatigued having had to work a double shift. After I gave the guy the pizza he went to the back to get some change. I took a look around. A strange guy stood near me staring deeply into my eyes. He was a middle aged guy, looking rather bedraggled and underfed, dressed in an over-worn raincoat and a threadbare cap. There was a wry smile on his aloof face and I couldn’t help envision him a kindhearted simpleton who probably had a burgeoning drinking problem and a wife who bullied him at home, routinely dragging him out of the pub by his ear. There was nothing youthful about him. He looked to be in his early to mid 40s and looked like the kind of guy with a lot of regrets in life. Then I heard the voice of the customer returning. I saw that someone dressed and looking eerily similar to the customer was near the simpleton while the customer himself was in front of me at the exact same time. It then dawned upon me that I was looking at a mirror the whole time. It then dawned upon me that elder, kindhearted simpleton was me.
